newsitem.title: GERMANY: Palm-dlr on its own doesn't determine Buba policy.
newsitem.headline: Palm-dlr on its own doesn't determine Buba policy.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Guntram Palm said on Friday a further significant dollar rise would have to be closely monitored but that the dollar exchange rate alone did not determine the Bundesbank's monetary policy.
Palm also said he saw no reason now to depart from the Bundesbank's practice of conducting fixed interest-rate weekly tenders for securities repurchase agreements, or repos.

"Primarily and as a rule, we in the central bank council steer our monetary policy according to the development of the money supply for good reasons," Palm said in statements sent to Reuters in response to a set of questions.
"And we have seen it (money supply) come clearly closer to our target growth corridor this year," Palm said.
The Bundesbank's M3 target growth corridor is 3.5 percent to 6.5 percent for this year.
June M3 is expected to be released early next week and analysts predict annualised M3 growth for the month slowed to 6.8 percent or 6.9 percent from 7.0 percent in May.

Asked whether he saw a danger that a sustained dollar rate of 1.79 marks or 1.80 marks could increase inflationary pressures in Germany in the foreseeable future, Palm said: "The depreciation of a currency in itself always has an impact on import prices.

"But given that the economy is by no means foaming over, given continued labour market problems and the far-reaching consequences of companies boosting productivity and cutting costs, I see no appreciable deterioration of the domestic price climate at present.
"But if the dollar should significantly appreciate further, this would have to be followed closely as part of an overall view of indicators that are relevant for monetary policy.
"But the development of the dollar rate on its own by no means determines our monetary policy actions."
Asked if the Bundesbank could return to setting repo tenders at variable rates to give a signal to markets that the German economy is on course for solid growth, Palm said:
"The German economy is on a growth path. I see no need at present to change our proven strategy in monetary policy. And this strategy since February 1996 has been to set fixed-rate repos."
The repo rate has been fixed at 3.00 percent since August 1996. There has been market speculation recently that the Bundesbank may return to variable-rate repo tenders.
